dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Hello there, youngster. Have you attended the festival that the Yashiro Commission and Yae Publishing House have organized in Ritou?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: I've heard that it's very well done indeed and that it's been very popular amongst the youngsters. Even a store run by an old codger like myself got quite a lot of customers who came for the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Everyone's all dressed up to nines and in high spirits, to boot.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Which is good, of course, very good! It feels like Inazuma itself is growing younger once more, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Youngster, are you hungry already? Come and try some of Erika's cooking!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And who might you be?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: I'm the owner of this izakaya.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Feel free to order anything. Just place your order with Erika. As far as I'm concerned, her cooking is one of the best in Inazuma City.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've heard that you're a real big shot.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Hmm? Who told you that?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Haha, Erika must have been bragging about me again.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: To be honest, I did have a pretty stand-up reputation when I was at the Tenryou Commission. Though I'm retired now, Yoriki and Doushin still often come to me for advice.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Recently, even some major figures from headquarters have visited our store... It seems like there's something afoot in Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Yeah, come back anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're the owner, and you're drinking?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Why not? Sake in my hand, fine cuisine at my table... After a busy life like mine, I think I'm owed at least a drink or two.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: You keep up the good work yourself! And when you're the boss someday, you can live like me, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Inazuma is currently...

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Ah, you're still young, dear customer. What do you care about politics in Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Well, it's understandable. You are a traveler from afar, after all. It would be troublesome if you got stuck in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: If I must shed some light on the matter... the Tenryou Commission believes in the power of our Almighty Shogun. She definitely has her reasons for making her choices.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me more about Seishimaru.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're interested in this tale, are you, youngster?

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: I shan't hide it from you, then. Seishimaru was once a relative of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: His tale was the talk of the town back in the day — not that I'd expect any young people to know of it now, though.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: I've lived for several decades myself and seen my own fair share of things. In truth, real life is often more exciting than fiction, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still can't drink alcohol.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: That's because you are still young.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: There are also benefits to not drinking. You are still young, so there's no hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: Let's have some barbecued skewers. They're delicious even without the drinks.
